Abu Huraira foretells, from the Prophet, a time when Allah and His Apostle's asylum for the Dhimmis is outraged, and Allah makes them dare to refuse the Jizya.
At Siffin Sahl bin Hunaif recalls Hudaibiya, when Umar protested the terms to the Prophet and Abu Bakr, and after Surat al-Fath the Prophet told him it was a victory.
During the Quraish peace treaty Asma's pagan mother visits her hoping for a reward from her, and the Prophet tells Asma to keep good relations with her.
Before an Umrah the Meccans allow the Prophet three days with sheathed arms; he erases 'Apostle of Allah' from the treaty himself when Ali refuses, and leaves after three days.
When Uqba throws camel intestines on the prostrating Prophet, he invokes Allah against the Quraish chiefs he names, later all killed at Badr and thrown into a well.
Every betrayer will have a flag on the Day of Resurrection, fixed or shown so that he is recognised and his betrayal made known.
Conquering Mecca, the Prophet says there is no migration now, only Jihad and intention, and Mecca is a sanctuary whose plants and game are protected, except Idhkhir.
The Prophet tells Yemenis that first there was only Allah, His Throne over the water, then heavens and earth were created; once he described creation through to Paradise and Hell.
Allah says the son of Adam slights Him by claiming He has a son and disbelieves in Him by denying He will recreate him as He first created him.
When Allah completed creation, He wrote in His Book with Him on His Throne: 'My Mercy overpowers My Anger'.
Whoever unjustly takes even a span of land will have it encircling his neck down seven earths, or sink down the seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.
Time has returned to its form at the creation of heavens and earth: the year has twelve months, four sacred, Dhul-Qa'da, Dhul-Hijja and Muharram in succession, and Mudar's Rajab.
Sued by Arwa before Marwan, Sa'id bin Zaid denies wronging her, citing the Prophet: whoever unjustly takes a span of land will have it round his neck down seven earths.
The sun prostrates beneath the Throne and asks leave to rise, until told to rise in the west; the sun and moon will be folded up on Resurrection Day.
The sun and moon are two of Allah's signs, not eclipsed for anyone's death or life, so pray at eclipses; the Prophet prayed two long rak'at, each with two bowings.
The Prophet was granted victory by the easterly wind and 'Ad destroyed by the westerly; clouds made him anxious until rain fell, lest they bring a tormenting wind.

His body opened and washed with Zamzam, the Prophet rides Al-Buraq with Gabriel through seven heavens greeting prophets, sees Al-Bait-al-Ma'mur and Sidrat-ul-Muntaha, and fifty prayers are reduced to five.
Formed in the womb in forty-day stages, each person has an angel write his deeds, livelihood, death and whether blessed or wretched, and what is written decides his final deeds.
Gabriel announces in heaven whom Allah loves; angels talk in the clouds as devils eavesdrop for soothsayers, record Friday arrivals at the mosque, and Gabriel supports Hassan's verses.
Asked how revelation comes, the Prophet says the angel sometimes comes like a ringing bell, the hardest on him, and sometimes in a man's form and speaks to him.
Whoever spends a pair of things in Allah's cause will be called by Paradise's gatekeepers, and the Prophet hopes Abu Bakr will be among them.
Gabriel greets Aisha, descends only by Allah's order, reads the Quran in seven ways, leads five prayers and says those dying without associating others enter Paradise; angels come in shifts.
Angels do not enter a house with pictures or a dog; picture-makers will be punished, the Prophet tells Aisha over a pictured pillow; Zaid excepts embroidery on garments.
Angels pray for those awaiting prayer; Malik keeps Hell; the Prophet declines the Angel of the Mountains' offer to crush his people, and saw Gabriel's real form with 600 wings.
A wife who refuses her husband's call to bed, so that he sleeps angry, is cursed by the angels till morning.
After a pause in revelation the Prophet saw the Hira angel seated between sky and earth, fell down, asked his family to cover him, and 'O you wrapped up' came.
On the night of his Ascent the Prophet saw tall brown Moses, medium-height Jesus, Malik the keeper of Hell and the Dajjal; angels will guard Medina from the Dajjal.
After death each person is shown his place in Paradise or Hell morning and evening; the Prophet saw the poor most numerous in Paradise and women most numerous in Hell.
The Prophet dreams of Umar's palace in Paradise; its tents are hollow pearls, its joys beyond imagining, its first entrants shine like the full moon, and Sa'd's handkerchiefs surpass silk.
A lash's space in Paradise outweighs the world; one tree's shade outlasts a century's ride; it has lofty mansions, a wet-nurse for Ibrahim, and Ar-Raiyan gate for the fasting.
Hell's breaths cause severe heat and cold, and fever is from its heat; its fire is seventy times ours, and one who enjoined good but did evil circles in it.
Bewitched, the Prophet learns in a dream that Labid bin Al-A'sam worked the magic with a comb and hair placed in Dharwan's well, and Allah cures him.
Satan knots sleepers' heads, urinates in a late sleeper's ear, prompts 'who created your Lord?' and runs in people like blood; Allah's name and Ayat al-Kursi keep him away.
Satan flees the adhan, distracts the praying, touches newborns except Jesus, brings yawning and bad dreams, set Muslims against Muslims at Uhud, avoids Umar's path and lodges in noses overnight.
Raise your voice in the adhan, Abu Sa'id tells a man fond of sheep and desert, for every human, jinn or thing hearing it will testify for him.
The Prophet ordered snakes killed, especially those with two white lines or a short tail, which blind and cause abortion, but later forbade killing snakes living in houses.
A time will come when a man's best property is sheep he grazes on mountain tops and rain-fed pastures, fleeing with his religion from afflictions.
Disbelief's source is in the east and pride among camel and horse owners, gentleness among sheep owners; belief is Yemenite, harshness among Rabi'a and Mudar where Satan's two horns appear.
Roosters crow on seeing an angel, so ask Allah's blessing; donkeys bray on seeing Satan, so seek refuge; at nightfall keep children close and shut doors, which Satan cannot open.
A lost group of Israelites were, the Prophet thinks, cursed and changed into rats, since rats refuse she-camel milk but drink sheep's milk.
